• Family: Ailiidae (formerly in Schilbeidae)
  • Common name: Garua bachcha
  • Size: 70 cm (28 in)
  • Temperature: 22-24°C (71-75°F)
  • pH: 6.5-7.2
Asia: Throughout northern India, but not south of the Mahanadi River, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Nepal. Type locality: Fresh water rivers of the Gangetic provinces.
Inhabits large fresh water and tidal rivers. According to Jayaram (1963), this species is found in the same habitat as A. coila, i.e. large rivers with turbid water and a substrate of sand or mud.
Feeds on insects, shrimps, other crustaceans and small fish.

Etymology: The genus name Clupisoma: clupea, herring; soma, body, referring to the herring-shaped body. The specific name garua: local Bengali name for this catfish in India.

IUCN Red List: Although there is evidence that Clupisoma garua may be threatened with overfishing in some areas (e.g. southern West Bengal), current evidence indicates that it is still a widespread and abundant species. It is therefore assessed as Least Concern. However, given its widespread use as a food fish, close monitoring of harvest levels and its effects on population size is critically needed (IUCN 2010).
